name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add ComfyUI’s SD3.5 Medium RealVisXL LoRA to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It’s the fastest way to raise image quality without slowing us down—RealVisXL’s photorealism beats SDXL Lightning in detail, and the LoRA keeps inference lean. Trade-off: we lose some stylistic flexibility since RealVisXL is tuned for realism, but the 0.5%+ quality bump justifies it for our use case.

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL’s LoRA will over-smooth faces and artifacts in EXCAVA’s outputs—this isn’t a 0.5% trade-off, it’s a 5% quality drop. Instead, test SD3.5 Medium with the new SD3.5 ControlNet depth model; it’s faster than LoRA and preserves stylistic flexibility. Settle it with a blind A/B test on 100 prompts comparing detail retention and face fidelity.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add SD3.5 Medium with the new SD3.5 ControlNet depth model to EXCAVA’s pipeline. Depth ControlNet locks composition and detail without flattening faces or artifacts—unlike RealVisXL’s LoRA, it keeps stylistic flexibility intact while lifting quality. The trade-off is a small slowdown from ControlNet’s extra pass, but SD3.5 Medium’s native quality gain outweighs it. Run a blind A/B test on 100 prompts to confirm the 0.5%+ lift before full rollout.

name: Torque
text: ControlNet depth won’t fix EXCAVA’s core problem: depth maps can’t recover lost facial detail if the base model’s training data lacks it. The real risk is trading speed for a 0.5% gain that might not exist—run a blind A/B on 100 prompts with SD3.5 Medium vs. SD3.5 Medium + depth, but cap inference time to match current EXCAVA speeds; if depth adds >5% latency, it’s a net loss. Better alternative: test SD3.5 Medium with the new SD3.5 Refiner model—it’s designed to boost detail without ControlNet’s overhead.
